summary: SERVER+PIPELINE second pass over the overhaul branch. (1) Self-play/learn integration: API surface matches — 111 targeted vitest cases pass (self-play route, selfPlayRunner, gameApi, breakageReport, omnathSeam canary, learn routes); outcomes.timeouts is handled exactly once everywhere (aggregate, .txt, OutcomeSummary) with no double-count; the --export-trajectories JSONL matches PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md §4 field-for-field. One real gap: the overhaul's empty-deck guard landed CLI-only, so the Sim Center route still seeds setup-error pods. (2) SPELLBOOK HEADLINE: Commander Spellbook DOES publish an authoritative bulk export — https://json.commanderspellbook.com/variants.json.gz (24,191,473 B gz / 540,397,329 B raw, S3+CloudFront, regenerated nightly — Last-Modified today 03:29 UTC; consumed by the official site repo and CubeCobra). I downloaded and stream-parsed the real file: {timestamp, version, variants:[95,001 status-OK records], aliases:[1,244 {id,variant} stubs]}; every field stripVariant reads (uses[].card.{name,oracleId}, produces[].feature.name, bracketTag, popularity, identity, manaValueNeeded) is present. Critical constraint verified: the decompressed doc (540,397,329 B) EXCEEDS Node's max string length (536,870,888), so the sync must stream-gunzip + record-split, never whole-file JSON.parse. Implementation-ready bulk-first design included; replaces the ~9.4k-variants-per-429-run paged crawl (~10% of the dataset shipped today) with a <2-min complete sync. (3) Release workflow: only overhaul change is sync-spellbook.yml → windows-2025 (correct, cache versions are OS-scoped); branch lint (eslint . --max-warnings 0) exits 0; found one adjacent strict-guard hole (index/cards files not REQUIRED) that can ship green-but-gutted combo features on cache eviction.

findings.what: Bundled Spellbook combo snapshot is ~10% of the real dataset because sync-spellbook.cjs pages a 429-throttled API; Commander Spellbook publishes an official bulk export that eliminates the cap — switch downloadVariants() to bulk-first with paged-resume fallback.
findings.evidence: Current: app/scripts/sync-spellbook.cjs:227 `const url = \`${BASE_URL}/variants?limit=${PAGE_SIZE}&offset=${offset}\`` (PAGE_SIZE 100, DELAY_MS 750, 429 sleep at :100-110); docs/orchestration/overhaul-evidence.md:96 "each run adds ~9.4k then 429s" and :30 "v0.84.0 shipped … 9,900 Spellbook combos". Bulk verified LIVE: HEAD https://json.commanderspellbook.com/variants.json → 200, Content-Length 540397329, Last-Modified Thu, 02 Jul 2026 03:29:44 GMT, ETag, Accept-Ranges: bytes, Server AmazonS3/CloudFront; variants.json.gz → Content-Length 24191473. Authoritative precedent: SpaceCowMedia/commander-spellbook-site src/services/bulk-api.service.ts uses `https://json.commanderspellbook.com/variant_id_map.json`; dekkerglen/CubeCobra packages/jobs/src/update_combos.ts:139 `const bulkUrl = 'https://json.commanderspellbook.com/variants.json.gz'`. I downloaded the gz and stream-parsed ALL of it: top-level `{"timestamp": "2026-07-02T03:29:35.948769+00:00", "version": "5.4.10", "variants": [...], "aliases": [...]}`; 95,001 variant records (every one status "OK") + 1,244 alias stubs shaped `{"id": "3011-5342", "variant": null}`. Variant keys (single signature across all 95,001): id,status,uses,requires,produces,of,includes,identity,manaNeeded,manaValueNeeded,easyPrerequisites,notablePrerequisites,description,notes,popularity,spoiler,bracketTag,legalities,prices,variantCount. Sample record: `{"id": "1580-4556-4871-6797", "status": "OK", "uses": [{"card": {"id": 4556, "name": "Blight Mound", "oracleId": "c4fe854e-8783-492e-bb2e-9f242ada8a5b", ...}, "zoneLocations": ["B"], "quantity": 1}, ...], "produces": [{"feature": {"id": 7, "name": "Infinite death triggers", ...}, "quantity": 1}, ...], "identity": "B", "manaValueNeeded": 0, "popularity": 23, "bracketTag": "E", "legalities": {"commander": true, ...}, "prices": {...}, "variantCount": 612}` — a strict superset of everything stripVariant (sync-spellbook.cjs:143-159) reads. LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT (verified by arithmetic on the live Content-Length): decompressed size 540,397,329 B > Node's max string length 2^29−24 = 536,870,888 — `fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8')`/one-shot `JSON.parse` throws ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG, so the bulk path MUST stream.
findings.fix: In sync-spellbook.cjs add BULK_URL = "https://json.commanderspellbook.com/variants.json.gz" and make downloadVariants() bulk-first: (1) fetch(BULK_URL) → Readable.fromWeb(res.body).pipe(zlib.createGunzip()) → a ~40-line brace-depth record splitter (track inString/escape; a record opens at depth 2 after the first depth-1 '['; JSON.parse each ~6 KB record substring — no new deps, never materialize the 515 MB doc; capture the doc's timestamp/version from the pre-array header text). (2) Per record: skip unless Array.isArray(rec.uses) (drops the 1,244 alias stubs) and rec.status === "OK"; map through the EXISTING stripVariant unchanged (field mapping verified above). (3) Accumulate stripped variants (~95k × ~600 B ≈ 50 MB — fine), then write ONCE via the existing atomic writeJson: COMBOS_FILE (stripped array), INDEX_FILE (existing buildIndex), META_FILE via writeMeta extended with { source: BULK_URL, bulkTimestamp, bulkVersion } (additive keys; getSpellbookMeta consumers read syncedAt/variants/cards only). Same three output files, same shapes — spellbook.js loadData/findCombos/estimateBracket untouched. (4) Wrap the bulk path in try/catch: any failure logs honestly and falls through to the EXISTING paged downloadVariants loop (resume logic untouched); add a --paged flag to force the old path. (5) downloadCards() stays paged (bulk uses[].card objects carry no gameChanger/tutor/massLandDenial/extraTurn flags — verified in the sample; /cards is ~1/10 the pages). Effects: release.yml's 12-min --combos-only step completes in <2 min with the FULL 95k dataset (CloudFront, no 429s); weekly workflow unchanged. Note downstream sizes: combos file grows ~9.9k→95k variants (~50 MB JSON + ~10-15 MB index; installer grows a few MB post-LZMA; spellbook.js lazy-loads on first combo call, one-time ~1 s parse). Optional trims (both safe): drop cardIds from stripVariant (zero consumers in app/src — grepped) and/or filter rec.legalities.commander === true (the tool is Commander-only).

findings.what: The overhaul's empty-deck guard landed in the CLI only — /api/self-play (the Sim Center UI path) still seeds empty/unenrichable decks into pods, reproducing the exact setup-error failure the branch just fixed.
findings.evidence: app/scripts/self-play.mjs:91-97 (added this branch): "EMPTY-DECK GUARD (overhaul pass): an empty/unenrichable deck ('Test Deck', a failed import) seeded 4-player pods that could only setup-error — 2 of 3 pods in a 10-deck sweep died on it" + `runnerDecks = runnerDecks.filter((d) => d.cards.length > 0);`. The route has no equivalent: app/src/app/api/self-play/route.js:144 `const runnerDecks = rawDecks.map(toRunnerDeck);` feeds runSelfPlayBatch directly, and route.js:135 `rawDecks = rawDecks.slice(0, mode === "commander" ? 4 : 2)` can slice an empty deck into the single "pod"-scope table. The UI makes this easy to hit: SimCenter.jsx:145 `const toggleAll = () => setSelectedIds(allSelected ? [] : decks.map((d) => d.id));` selects every deck across every profile. route.test.js has no empty-deck case (grepped).
findings.fix: Apply the same guard in the route after enrichment: filter `d.cards.length === 0` out of runnerDecks BEFORE the pod-scope slice (move the slice after enrichment, or enrich-then-filter-then-slice), return 400 if nothing playable remains, and surface the skipped names honestly in the response (e.g. `skippedDecks: [names]`) so the UI can show them — mirroring the CLI's console.warn. Better long-term: hoist the filter into a shared helper in selfPlayDecks.js so both callers can't drift again (the file's own header says it exists so "the deck→runner transformation lives in exactly one place").

findings.what: Strict bundle guard requires spellbook-combos but NOT spellbook-index/spellbook-cards — a cache-evicted release passes strict yet ships combos that can never load (index missing) or a dead bracket estimator (cards missing).
findings.evidence: app/scripts/prepare-tauri-resources.cjs:167-174 REQUIRED_DATA lists only "data/spellbook-combos.local.json" of the four Spellbook files. But app/src/lib/server/spellbook.js:65 `if (!fs.existsSync(combosFile) || !fs.existsSync(indexFile)) { console.warn(...); return false; }` — combos without index ⇒ findCombos permanently `ready:false`; and spellbook.js:242 `if (!_cards) return { bracketTag: "unknown", ... ready: false }`. release.yml:146 runs `node scripts/sync-spellbook.cjs --combos-only`, and sync-spellbook.cjs:321 `if (!COMBOS_ONLY) { await downloadCards(); }` — so the release NEVER writes spellbook-cards.local.json itself; it arrives only via the refdata- cache restore from the weekly job. Cache eviction under the 10 GB quota is the documented failure mode that already shipped ~68 gutted releases (release.yml:136-141 comment).
findings.fix: Add "data/spellbook-index.local.json" to REQUIRED_DATA — it is written in the same per-page loop as combos (sync-spellbook.cjs:236-237), so requiring it adds no new failure surface and closes the combos-present-but-unloadable hole. For cards: once the F1 bulk switch frees the 12-min budget, drop --combos-only from the release step (paged /cards is ~1/10 the volume of variants) and add "data/spellbook-cards.local.json" to REQUIRED_DATA too; until then, at minimum log a ::warning in the release step when the cards file is absent so a bracket-dead bundle is visible in the run log.

findings.what: The bounded release Spellbook step (12-min timeout) can kill sync-spellbook.cjs between its per-page COMBOS/INDEX writes and before writeMeta — the bundle then ships an index one page behind combos and a stale meta that under-reports the snapshot.
findings.evidence: sync-spellbook.cjs:236-237 writes COMBOS_FILE then INDEX_FILE inside the page loop, and writeMeta (line 325) runs only after the full loop completes; release.yml:145 `timeout-minutes: 12` + `continue-on-error: true` around `node scripts/sync-spellbook.cjs --combos-only`. A timeout mid-loop leaves combos fresher than index (extra combos unreachable via _index — an honest miss, no false positive) and spellbook-meta.local.json still holding the restored snapshot's counts, so /api/knowledge-status (SPELLBOOK_META_PATH, knowledge-status/route.js:15) understates what actually shipped.
findings.fix: PARK — fully mooted by the F1 bulk switch (bulk completes in <2 min and always reaches writeMeta; its single-shot write also makes combos/index/meta atomic as a set). Only if bulk is rejected: update META_FILE inside the page loop alongside the other two writes.

findings.what: SimCenter's backend-surface docstring omits the `scope` key it actually sends, drifting the documented /api/self-play POST contract.
findings.evidence: app/src/components/mtg/SimCenter.jsx:24 documents `POST /api/self-play → run; body { deckIds, mode, gamesPer, allProfiles, record }` while the fetch at SimCenter.jsx:175 sends `scope` too, and route.js:112 consumes it (`const scope = body?.scope === "pod" ? "pod" : "all";`).
findings.fix: One-line doc fix: add `scope` to the documented body. Fold into the F2 change.

findings.what: The overhaul's own pod-aware combat naming (N2) degrades to raw engine seat ids for most of a pod game: the defender label falls back to t.defenderId ('ai1') whenever the defending seat's command zone is empty — which is true from the moment that opponent casts their commander until it dies. Beginner narration and the board-mode attack buttons read 'Attack ai1 with [[Grizzly Bears]]'. In Standard 1v1 with an enemy planeswalker (the other multi-target trigger) the label is ALWAYS 'ai' since Standard seats have no commander at all.
findings.evidence: app/src/lib/learn/legalChoices.js:1645 `const defenderName = state.players[t.defenderId]?.command?.[0]?.name || t.defenderId;` — and `command` is the live command zone (app/src/lib/learn/cmdCast.test.js:70 pins `expect(s.players.user.command.find(...)).toBeUndefined(); // left the command zone`). Narrator's own nice fallback never fires because defenderName is truthy: app/src/lib/learn/narrator.js:230 `const defenderName = action.defenderName || (action.defenderId ? seatLabel(action.defenderId) : null);`. Live probe: narrateAction with defenderName:'ai1' → "Attack ai1 with [[Grizzly Bears]]."; with defenderName undefined → "Attack Opponent 1 with [[Grizzly Bears]]." LearnBoard button also renders it raw: app/src/components/mtg/LearnBoard.jsx:281 `Attack ${o.targetName || o.defenderName || o.defenderId || ""} with ${o.name}`.
findings.fix: In actionsDeclareAttacker, resolve the defender's commander name across zones, else emit null so the narrator's seatLabel supplies 'Opponent N': `const seat = state.players[t.defenderId]; const defenderName = seat?.command?.[0]?.name || seat?.battlefield?.find(p => p.card?.isCommander)?.card?.name || null;` (spread `...(defenderName ? { defenderName } : {})`). In LearnBoard.jsx add the same SEAT_LABELS map LearnView already has (LearnView.jsx:68) and render `o.targetName || o.defenderName || SEAT_LABELS[o.defenderId] || ""`. Add a narrator.test.js case pinning that a cast-commander pod seat narrates as 'Opponent 1', not 'ai1'.

findings.what: Board mode caps the clickable action buttons at 6 while the overhaul's new expandable narration panel (N6) lists ALL numbered actions — in pod combat (attackers × 3 defenders (+ planeswalkers) = easily 9+ actions) the beginner reads 'Your legal actions: 1..9' in the panel but can only click the first 6. E.g. with 3 attackers you cannot declare creature #3's attack first; you must route through one of the first 6 buttons. Board mode is the only shipped Academy UI (the N6 commit itself states routes always send a boardSnapshot, so the text-mode DecisionPrompt never renders).
findings.evidence: app/src/components/mtg/LearnBoard.jsx:277 `{options.filter(o => o.kind !== "pass-priority" && o.kind !== "tap-for-mana").slice(0, 6).map((o, i) => (` — hard cap, no overflow affordance. Meanwhile the same decision's prompt from narrateDecision numbers every action (app/src/lib/learn/narrator.js:403-409 `const lines = actions.map((action, i) => ... `${i + 1}. ${description}`)`) and the new lb-narrpanel (LearnBoard.jsx:296-303) renders all of them as text. The cap predates the branch, but the overhaul's clickable narration now advertises actions the bar cannot dispatch — an integration gap the first pass missed.
findings.fix: Make lb-actions scrollable without the slice (the container already has `overflow-x:auto;max-width:42%` at LearnBoard.jsx CSS `.lb-actions`), i.e. drop `.slice(0, 6)`; or raise the cap and add a '+N more' button that opens the full action list as a tappable overlay (reuse the lb-narrpanel shell, one button per action calling onAction). Dropping the slice is the minimal correct fix since the row already scrolls.

findings.what: wardCostLabel's rendered mana pips get run through .toLowerCase() in the body copy of both new/updated payment panels, so a colored/hybrid cost renders as 'You may pay {2}{g}' / 'will be countered unless you pay {1}{w/u}' — wrong mana-symbol case, ironically in the exact colored-pip cases wardCostLabel was added to render correctly (the legacy generic '{3}' path is digit-only and unaffected).
findings.evidence: app/src/components/mtg/LearnView.jsx:1343 `will be countered unless you {costLabel.toLowerCase()}.` (SoftCounterPanel), :1388 `✨ You may {costLabel.toLowerCase()}{...}` and :1391 `You may {costLabel.toLowerCase()}. If you do, the effect resolves.` (OptionalManaPaymentPanel). wardCostLabel (LearnView.jsx:38-53) emits uppercase pips: `for (const c of ["W", "U", "B", "R", "G", "C"]) ... pips.push(`{${c}}`)`.
findings.fix: Lowercase only the verb, never the pips: `const inline = costLabel.replace(/^Pay/, "pay");` and interpolate `{inline}` at all three sites. (Life costs — 'pay 3 life' — are unaffected either way.)

findings.what: In Standard 1v1 (the fast path: lone opponent, no enemy planeswalker) declare-attacker actions carry no defender fields, so the new board-bar label renders 'Attack  with Grizzly Bears' — double space, dangling 'Attack' with no object.
findings.evidence: app/src/lib/learn/legalChoices.js:1629-1635 fast path emits `{ kind: "declare-attacker", playerId, permanentId: p.id, name: p.card.name }` (no defenderName/defenderId/targetName); app/src/components/mtg/LearnBoard.jsx:281 renders `Attack ${o.targetName || o.defenderName || o.defenderId || ""} with ${o.name}` → `Attack  with X`.
findings.fix: Build the target segment conditionally: `const tgt = o.targetName || o.defenderName || SEAT_LABELS[o.defenderId]; return tgt ? `Attack ${tgt} with ${o.name}` : `Attack with ${o.name}`;` (folds into finding 1's edit at the same line).

findings.what: The tableSnapshot commander-mirror disambiguation suffix leaks the raw seat id into the UI: two same-name commanders produce commander-damage rows labeled 'Koma, Cosmos Serpent (ai1)' in the TableStrip (rendered above the board in BOTH board and text modes). Functionally correct (rows no longer last-write-win into one) but the '(ai1)' suffix is a raw engine id shown to the user.
findings.evidence: app/src/lib/learn/tableSnapshot.js:45 `const label = info ? (nameSeen[info.name] > 1 ? `${info.name} (${info.seat})` : info.name) : cmdId;` — seat is the raw pid ('ai1'). Rendered at app/src/components/mtg/LearnView.jsx:738 `cmd.map(([from, n]) => `${seatLabel(from)} ${n}`)` where seatLabel passes unknown keys through unchanged (LearnView.jsx:70 `return SEAT_LABELS[id] || id;`), so the composite name+suffix string is displayed verbatim. TableStrip mounts unconditionally at LearnView.jsx:393.
findings.fix: Map the seat through a label table server-side in tableSnapshot.js: `const SEAT_LABEL = { user: "you", ai: "opponent", ai1: "opponent 1", ai2: "opponent 2", ai3: "opponent 3" }; ... `${info.name} (${SEAT_LABEL[info.seat] || info.seat})`` → 'Koma, Cosmos Serpent (opponent 1)'. Update tableSnapshot.test.js's mirror expectation accordingly.

findings.what: LearnBoard renders raw engine seat ids in five user-facing spots, and the opponent summary tile loses its name AND commander art for most of the game: the tile label is `o.command?.[0]?.name || o.id`, and the command zone empties the moment that opponent casts their commander — so mid-game the right rail shows tiles literally titled 'ai1'/'ai2'/'ai3' with no art, the focus header says "ai1's Battlefield", the back bar says '(viewing ai1)', and every game-log line opens with 'ai1 ·'. Pre-existing, but board mode is the shipped Academy surface and this is the same root cause as finding 1 (live command zone used as a seat-name source).
findings.evidence:
app/src/components/mtg/LearnBoard.jsx:226 `
{o.command?.[0]?.name || o.id}
` (+ :224 art keys off `o.command[0]` too); :142 `(viewing {focused.id})`; :197 and :208 `${focused.id}'s` Battlefield/Lands; :236 `{e.actor}...` in the game log. Command zone emptiness on cast pinned by app/src/lib/learn/cmdCast.test.js:70.
findings.fix: Add a per-player display label server-side in boardSnapshot.js (it already walks each player): `commanderName` resolved across zones (command zone → battlefield/graveyard/exile isCommander card) plus a `label` ('You'/'Opponent N'). LearnBoard then uses `o.commanderName || o.label` for tiles (art from commanderName), `focused.label` for the header/back-bar, and maps `e.actor` through the same labels. One server change fixes all five spots and keeps finding 1's fix consistent.

findings.what: The pause-time decision for every pendingChoice kind spreads the whole pendingChoice into the wire response — including the `resume` continuation (full remaining atom program, targets, context) and `effectAtoms` — so /api/learn/choose//step responses ship internal engine program state to the browser on every interactive pause. No hidden info leaks (all sourced from public cards) and nothing breaks (plain JSON by construction), but it bloats every pause response and freezes internal atom shapes into the de-facto wire contract the Omnath play-API work is trying to lock down.
findings.evidence: app/src/lib/learn/learnSession.js:1160 `return { session: current, decision: { kind: "optional-mana-payment", ...pc, affordable } };` (same `...pc` spread at every pause branch, e.g. :1088, :1104); pc carries `resume: { program, controller, targets, xValue, sourceId, context, ... }` attached at app/src/lib/learn/effects/runProgram.js:114/135, and routes return the decision verbatim (app/src/app/api/learn/choose/route.js:74 `decision: enrichUnresolvedDecision(result.decision, stepped.state)`).
findings.fix: PARK or do as a small hygiene pass: introduce a `decisionView(pc, extras)` that whitelists the client-consumed fields per kind (kind, controller, sourceName, cost/amount, subtype, available/affordable, candidates, spellName, cardName, zone) and strips `resume`/`effectAtoms`. Park-worthy because it touches all 13 pause branches and the client contract should be changed in one deliberate pass, coordinated with the PLAY-API contract work (P3 item 2-3) rather than inside this UI wave.

summary: UI/CLIENT second pass over the overhaul branch (v0.84.0..HEAD; UI delta = LearnBoard.jsx, LearnView.jsx, SelfPlayPanel.jsx, useLearnSession.js + 3 learn routes). VERIFIED CLEAN: (1) all three new panels (OptionalManaPaymentPanel, OptionalSacPanel, + CommanderReturnPanel wiring) are wired end-to-end — panel → session hook → wire kind-echo (WI-5) → applyPendingChoice dispatch, field names match the server pendingChoice shapes (cost/affordable, subtype/available), and every one of the 13 pendingChoice kinds has a board-mode side-sheet; (2) SelfPlayPanel/SimCenter timeout accounting is consistent and does NOT double-count — `timeouts` matches breakageReport's bucket, is excluded from `completed`, and appears once in the non-completions row; the /api/self-play route is unchanged on this branch; (3) chat/deck surfaces (deck switch, busy scope, SSE watchdog) are untouched by the branch — zero component/lib changes outside learn — so no overhaul interaction exists; (4) 218 targeted vitest cases across the touched seams all pass (SelfPlayPanel, SimCenter, pendingChoiceUiWiring, pendingChoiceKindEcho, pendingChoiceKinds, narrator, tableSnapshot, learnSession, optionalManaPayment, reflexiveSacBySubtype, breakageReport). FOUND: 1×P1 — the N2 pod-combat naming falls back to raw seat ids ('Attack ai1 with [[Grizzly Bears]]') for most of a pod game because it reads the LIVE command zone (empties on commander cast; probe-confirmed through the narrator), and always in Standard-with-planeswalker games; 1×P2 — the board bar's hard `.slice(0, 6)` now conflicts with the N6 clickable narration that lists every numbered action (pod combat routinely exceeds 6); 5×P3 polish/park items (lowercased mana pips via costLabel.toLowerCase(), 'Attack  with X' in the 1v1 fast path, raw '(ai1)' mirror suffix in commander-damage rows, five raw-seat-id renders in LearnBoard incl. opponent tiles losing name+art mid-game, and the `...pc` pause spread shipping `resume` program state over the wire — recommend PARK/coordinate with the PLAY-API contract).

RUST SHELL + BUILD PIPELINE second pass: no fresh regressions and no P0/P1 found. (1) lib.rs is clippy/fmt-clean by inspection — cfg-gating is consistent (`#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] use std::net::TcpStream` matches its only consumer `wait_for_port`; both Windows-only helpers `pin_child_to_job`/`reap_orphan_servers` are gated `all(target_os="windows", not(debug_assertions))` with matching call-site attributes); the overhaul branch (v0.84.0..HEAD) never touched app/src-tauri, next.config.mjs, or package.json (`git diff --stat` shows only sync-spellbook.yml +5 and self-play.mjs +52). (2) Bundle allowlist is tight: prepare-tauri-resources.cjs stages only the explicit `dataFiles` list (16 entries) guarded by `REQUIRED_DATA` strict-set of 6 (fails CI=true builds), the 8-name `syncScripts` list ("sync-scryfall-bulk.cjs","sync-spellbook.cjs","sync-edhrec-salt.cjs","sync-scryfall-oracle.cjs","build-oracle-index.cjs","build-collection-printings-index.cjs","build-rules-index.cjs","sync-cardkingdom-prices.cjs"), and knowledge md filtered to `name.startsWith("L") || name.startsWith("META_")`. The new overhaul scripts (play-quality-probe.mjs, qa-sweep.mjs, allowlist-guard.mjs, program/runtime-fingerprint.mjs, self-play.mjs) and docs are NOT staged and are referenced from runtime src only in comments (grep verified); .next/standalone is copied wholesale but strip-standalone-bloat.cjs removes standalone/data + standalone/knowledge. Every runtime `dataPath("...")` consumer (cardIndex, printingIndex, rulesRetrieval, spellbook, edhrecSalt, cardKingdomPrices, knowledge-status, collection/prices) maps to a bundled dataFiles entry; /api/sync-data's 7 STEP_SCRIPTS are all in syncScripts. (3) next.config.mjs/package.json: nothing stale; versionAlignment.test.js + paths.test.js pass (7/7, vitest run). Only blemish = a 2-space indentation glitch on the "build:seed-prices" script line. (4) self-play.mjs --export-trajectories CANNOT hit the read-only resources dir in a packaged .exe: the script is not in the syncScripts bundle allowlist so it doesn't exist inside the .exe; its default report path is `path.join(appRoot(), "data", "self-play", ...)` where appRoot() = MTG_APP_ROOT (lib.rs:439 sets it to the writable %APPDATA% dir); the trajectory path is an explicit `path.resolve(args.exportTrajectories)` user arg; and paths.js's bundled fallback (dataPath, paths.js:105-113) is read-only by construction — it returns the MTG_REFERENCE_DIR path only when the file already EXISTS there, and self-play.mjs never routes writes through dataPath anyway. The in-.exe /api/self-play banking path uses profilePath("self-play","trajectories") which always resolves under detectAppRoot() (paths.js:181-185), never the reference dir. Also verified: the branch's one CI change (sync-spellbook.yml ubuntu→windows-2025) is coherent — the `shell: bash` summary step works on Windows runners, and the refdata- cache prefix now OS-matches release.yml's restore. Trajectory-export integration (4999bdd) is sound: selfPlayRunner returns decisionTrajectory/winnerSeat/onThePlay/trainingWeight exactly as self-play.mjs consumes them, and `"--export-trajectories=".length` = 22 matches the slice(22). Three P3 findings below (one is the assignment-requested design for parked #6).

findings.what: Cargo.toml version (0.3.0) drifts from tauri.conf.json/package.json (0.84.0) — WAKE-REPORT parked #6; assignment asked for the minimal fix design. The drift is cosmetic: Tauri 2 uses tauri.conf.json's "version" (which CI re-syncs from the release tag) for the bundle, updater, and app.getVersion(), and versionAlignment.test.js guards package.json ↔ tauri.conf.json only.
findings.evidence: app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:3 `version = "0.3.0"` vs app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:4 `"version": "0.84.0"`; .github/workflows/release.yml:64-79 rewrites ONLY tauri.conf.json from the tag (`$conf.version = $version`); app/src/lib/versionAlignment.test.js:21-22 checks only `readJson("package.json")` vs tauri.conf.json; installed .exe reports 0.84.0 via `app.getVersion()` (UpdatesModal.jsx:159) proving tauri.conf wins.
findings.fix: Comment-only (do NOT bump per release). Add above the version line in app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml: `# NOT the shipped app version: tauri.conf.json "version" (synced from the release tag by release.yml) overrides this for the bundle, updater, and app.getVersion(); versionAlignment.test.js guards package.json <-> tauri.conf.json. Frozen deliberately - bumping per release would only churn Cargo.lock and the CI cargo-cache key (release.yml keys on hashFiles('app/src-tauri/Cargo.lock')) for zero user-visible effect.` Optionally add one line to versionAlignment.test.js's docstring noting Cargo.toml is deliberately excluded. Rejecting the CI-rewrite alternative: extending the version-sync step to Cargo.toml would dirty Cargo.lock mid-build and break the exact-match cargo cache key.

findings.what: wait_for_port() treats ANY listener on 127.0.0.1:3000 as "our server is ready" — a bare TcpStream::connect probe. If a foreign process holds port 3000, the spawned bundled Node dies with EADDRINUSE (logged only to server.err.log) while the shell logs `port 3000 ready = true` and the webview redirects into the foreign app. Pre-existing since v0.1 (not an overhaul regression); reap_orphan_servers already removes the most likely squatter (our own orphaned node.exe), so real-world likelihood on a single-user desktop is low.
findings.evidence: app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:40-50 `fn wait_for_port(port: u16, ...) { ... if TcpStream::connect(&addr).is_ok() { return true; } ... }` and lib.rs:462 `let ready = wait_for_port(3000, 30);` — no identity check; lib.rs:117 `reap_orphan_servers` only kills processes whose image path is byte-for-byte the bundled node.exe (lib.rs:112-115 SAFETY comment), so a non-MTG port-3000 app survives and gets loaded by the placeholder redirect.
findings.fix: PARK (pre-existing across ~84 shipped releases; port is hardcoded end-to-end incl. next.config CSP and the placeholder redirect, so a fix is a cross-cutting change). If ever picked up: after spawn, verify identity instead of liveness — poll `child.try_wait()` alongside wait_for_port and log an explicit `port 3000 already in use by another app` line when the child exits nonzero within the wait window (read server.err.log tail for EADDRINUSE), so launch.log diagnoses it in one glance; a full fix would probe an app-identifying endpoint (e.g. GET /api/knowledge-status) rather than a raw TCP connect.

findings.what: RELEASE.md's key-rotation runbook uses the BOM-injecting PowerShell pipe that gotcha #12 and CLAUDE.md §3.5 explicitly forbid — following it during a rotation sets a corrupted TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret and breaks CI signing at the exact moment you can least afford it.
findings.evidence: RELEASE.md:84: `Get-Content $env:USERPROFILE\.tauri\mtg-tool.key -Raw | gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY --repo Robak503/mtg-tool` — vs docs/gotchas.md:62-64: "PowerShell pipes add UTF-8 BOMs when piping Get-Content to gh secret set. Use cmd /c \"gh secret set X < file\" instead" and CLAUDE.md §3.5: "IMPORTANT: use cmd /c with < redirect, NOT PowerShell pipe — pipes add UTF-8 BOM".
findings.fix: Replace step 2 of 'Rotating signing keys' with the sanctioned pattern: `cmd /c "gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY --repo Robak503/mtg-tool < %USERPROFILE%\.tauri\mtg-tool.key"` (and add the same for TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD, which the rotation section never mentions updating).
